submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires retrospectively on gradable-property predications: the degree words ' so', ' too', ' much' and ' more' when they grade an adjective or adverb ('so hot', 'too fast', 'too much', 'more polite', 'so much'), the adjective or adverb being graded (' fast', ' hard', ' close', ' wide', ' dark', ' little', ' bit', ' much'), the copular and change-of-state verbs that introduce a gradable predicate (' look' in 'look nice' or 'look bad', ' feel' in 'feel happy' or 'feel strange', ' turned' in 'turned to a frown', ' becoming' in 'becoming stiff', ' not' in 'to not be scared'), and ' so' in 'so that' purpose clauses. It does not fire on other intensifiers (' very', ' really', ' extremely', ' quite', ' rather', ' pretty'), on ' too' meaning 'also', on ' more' as a plain noun quantifier, on ' much' as a pronoun or after 'very', on plain adjectives and adverbs with no degree word, on ' look' as a perception verb, on ' turned' for physical turning, on ' so' as a result connective or in 'think so', or on sentence-initial 'So', and it does not prepare any upcoming token.
